sources.citation: Sanjoko, Yohanis. 2016. Analisis konstrastif fonem bahasa Kanum Sota dan bahasa Kanum Barkari. Kibas Cenderawasih 13(1): 1-16. DOI 10.26499/kc.v13i1.97
sources.note: Segmental comparison only (inventories, contrasts, distributions of Kanum Sota vs Kanum Barkari, based on Sanjoko 2014 and Iribaram 2015). 'tekanan (stress)' occurs once, p.3, in a generic textbook definition of suprasegmentals (Lapoliwa 1988); nothing language-specific about stress.

sources.citation: Iribaram, Siti Masitha. 2015. Fonem segmental bahasa Kanum Barkari. Gramatika: Jurnal Ilmiah Kebahasaan dan Kesastraan 3(1): 47-59. Ternate: Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Maluku Utara.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Companion Balai Bahasa phonology of the neighbouring Kanum Barkari (Naukenjerai) variety written from the same 2014 fieldwork programme; if it has a suprasegmental paragraph it would be the closest proxy, though it is not Sota Kanum.
sources.venue: Gramatika: Jurnal Ilmiah Kebahasaan dan Kesastraan

sources.citation: Sanjoko, Yohanis. 2014. Fonem segmental bahasa Kanum Sota. Kibas Cenderawasih 11(2): 139-150. Jayapura: Balai Bahasa Provinsi Papua dan Papua Barat. DOI 10.26499/kc.v11i2.161
sources.note: No suprasegmental/stress section (secs. 4.1 sound inventory, 4.2 contrasts and allophones, 4.3 distribution, 4.4 syllable patterns V/VK/KV/KVK/KKV/KKVK, 4.5 clusters, 5 conclusion). Stress appears only as a conditioning environment for allophones on pp.144-145: /n m ŋ/ and /a e i/ realised differently 'pada suku kata terbuka yang (tidak) mendapat tekanan' (in open syllables that do / do not receive stress), e.g. /a/ -> [a:] in a stressed open syllable, [a] in an unstressed open syllable. Presupposes word stress; never says which syllable carries it; transcriptions carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Carroll, Matthew J. 2016. The Ngkolmpu language (PhD, ANU); Carroll 2021. Phonetics and phonology of Ngkolmpu (LD&C SP24) -- sister variety Ngkolmpu/Ngkâlmpw Kanum (ngka1235), already checked in
sources.note: Checked the existing ngka1235 check (A/B/): no stress placement rule stated for Ngkolmpu either (word stress presupposed; transcriptions trend initial). Different language-level glottocode; not usable for sota1242.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2015. Morphological opacity: rules of referral in Kanum verbs. In M. Baerman, D. Brown & G. Corbett (eds.), Understanding and Measuring Morphological Complexity, 69-92 (approx.). Oxford: OUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Donohue is the only linguist with extensive first-hand Kanum fieldwork besides Carroll; his chapters typically open with a phonology note. Caveat: his Kanum is usually the Ngkâlmpw/Yanggandur variety (ngka1235), so identity must be checked before use for sota1242.
